evidence.C1: First job cut to under a minute, but scripted test failed once: 'one did not finish (the car was wrecked in traffic)'.
evidence.C2: Strong neon night atmosphere, but day mode screenshots appear flatter and less distinct than night.
evidence.C3: Jobs, police, money sinks and secrets feed each other; 'Perks... tie the side activities together'.
evidence.C4: HUD is cash and health only; 'stars appear only when you are wanted', passes overlap tests.
evidence.C5: Fact sheet states 'No real players have tried it yet' and 'Own names only' confirmed by Gate 9.

fixes: Make the tutorial vehicle indestructible or add a 'Mission Failed' restart trigger to prevent players getting stuck if they crash (scripted test failed once).
Enhance day mode lighting and textures to match the atmospheric quality and distinct mood of the night cycle.
Add a specific early-game prompt connecting the $250 job reward to the first affordable upgrade or property to clarify the economy loop.

evidence.C1: Title screen shows six keys clearly with 'what changed' line; first job cut to under a minute ending at Sol Wheel pier; HUD reduced to cash and health; 'A new player who stands still for 3.5 seconds is shown the walking keys'. Still requires reading the title screen controls and the job prompt to proceed.
evidence.C2: Four districts with distinct palettes (Meridian aqua/coral, Sol Beach pastel, Rustport rust/ochre), 86 painted walls with district-specific designs, day/night cycle with lit windows and neon, Sol Wheel and Coastliner airship as landmarks. Screenshots show recognizable mood but city geometry remains somewhat generic blocky towers.
evidence.C3: Six story jobs, four odd-job types (Rush Order, Repo Run, Block Dash, Hot Parcel), cab fares with streak bonuses, four properties with rent, 15 hidden packages, harbor courier, Sol Wheel ride, tune-up shop in three stages, perks that cross-feed (5 packages -> 25% less damage, 10 fares -> double tips, all jobs -> +50% rent). 'Perks tie the side activities together'.
evidence.C4: HUD is cash and health only; stars appear only when wanted; weapon line for 5s after change; clock moved to map/pause; pause screen is three buttons plus settings and perks; map legend moved onto map; G8 no overlaps at three resolutions. Perk card shows progress like 'Body armour 4/5'.
evidence.C5: Own city/names (G9 passed), one 'not affiliated' line on title, fact sheet plainly states 'No real players have tried it yet', 'Only tested in Chrome on one Windows laptop; no phone or gamepad controls', 'Every other job, the cab fares and the courier shift are passed by script'. Limits and test coverage stated honestly.

fixes: Run the remaining five story jobs, cab fares, and courier shift through real key-press tests like test/drive.py does for the first job, so difficulty and time limits are measured by a human-paced driver rather than teleported between markers.

Get a small group of real players (even 3-5) to play for 10-15 minutes each and report where they got stuck, what felt unclear, and whether the synth radio and driving feel land; the fact sheet itself flags 'No real players have tried it yet' as the biggest unknown.

Strengthen the city's silhouette so it reads as Neon Coast from a single screenshot: add more varied rooflines, a second or third pier landmark, and district-specific skyline accents beyond the Sol Wheel and Spire, since the current skyline still leans on generic stepped towers.

evidence.C1: First view already shows 'Get into the red car ahead [F]' with 'JOB 111 m' and a minimap marker; first job 'cut... to under a minute' and 12 of 14 scripted runs finished in 38.9-51.2 s - but one ran 111.3 s and one ended with the car 'wrecked in traffic after 105.6 s', so the first minute can still go wrong for a stranger.
evidence.C2: '86 painted walls', district palettes ('aqua, coral, cream and lilac'), a 'glow pass' at night and the dusk Sol Wheel shot give a consistent, readable neon-beach mood by day and night; but buildings remain simple boxes with flat window grids, so the mood is pleasant rather than yet recognisable as its own from any one screenshot.
evidence.C3: Six story jobs, 'odd jobs come in four kinds', cab fares, property, 15 packages, wheel ride, tune-up; 'Perks... tie the side activities together' and 'Police heat now reaches the other systems' make them feed each other - docked because the side jobs' 'difficulty and their time limits are not measured' and odd jobs are 'taken in turn'.
evidence.C4: HUD cut to 'cash and health', stars only when wanted, weapon line for 5 s; G8 reports 'no overlaps at 3 sizes'; title 'shows six keys' with eight folded away - only the big-map legend (dense small coloured text) and the temporary perk card under the cash fall short of 'reads at a glance'.
evidence.C5: 'Own city, names and art' with G9 'own names only' and the single 'not affiliated' line; the 'Not covered by the tests' section states limits plainly - driving feel, script-passed jobs, one Chrome laptop, no phone/gamepad, 'No real players have tried it yet'.

fixes: Harden the first job against traffic: 2 of 14 scripted runs failed or overran (one car 'wrecked in traffic after 105.6 s'), so thin traffic on the beach road or make the first car wreck-proof/replaceable until the job ends - a stranger's first minute should not be able to end in a wreck.

Verify side-activity difficulty with real input: cab fares, the courier shift and the four odd-job types are only 'passed by script' with the car moved between markers, so their timers and difficulty are unmeasured - drive each once by key presses and tune the clocks.

Differentiate the city beyond painted fronts: add varied rooflines and block massing per district (beyond Meridian tiers and suburb pitches) so the world reads as its own place from any screenshot, not only the landmark shots.
